text: Six months from now, a blood-red sky hangs over Gwanghwamun, and an S-grade gate tears open above Seoul like a wound.
One man in a black coat walks straight toward it, and the livestream chat loses its mind. A summoner, going in first? Everyone knows summoners are bait.
Then you see what is behind him: seven strange shapes, from a stone giant to a cloaked goblin no taller than his waist.
The little goblin at his side looks up, deadpan, as if he already knows the answer.
The man doesn't even break stride.
The rule every guild once used on him, turned into a promise.
All seven leap into the gate, and the whole square shakes.
But six months earlier, he was the bait. Gate 0912: a C-grade gate at the bottom of a subway dig in Mapo, raided tonight by the Black Hound Guild.
Seven hunters, a rookie healer, and one trap-tester, paid per trap.
That trap-tester is our main character, Kang Jaeha. The raid leader reminds him of the rule, and Jaeha answers like a waiter: yes, sir. Summons go first.
His power is the weakest there is. He can call one thing: a husk, a faceless white doll that cannot fight. He even calls it a very brave husk.
The hunters have a name for him, and it isn't Kang Jaeha.
Inside is a ruined fortress under a sick green sky, and the husk walks ahead of everyone.
It steps on the wrong stone.
Spikes burst from both walls, and the husk shatters like a dropped plate.
To them, his whole life is worth less than one bottle from a guild shop.
Kang Jaeha, twenty-four. F-rank. Three hundred and twelve raids, zero kills. He just smiles and dusts off his notebook, because every party he walks in front of comes home.
Because while they laugh, he writes down everything that tries to kill them.
Minutes later, a pack of stone lizards rounds the corner, and the first one bites the tank's shield.
He's counting. And the frozen rookie healer is standing exactly where the tail will land.
She does, and the tail smashes the wall right where her face was.
Song Yerin, twenty, E-rank healer, first raid. She wants to know how he knew.
Jaeha shrugs it off. Being underestimated is the only armour he has.
Then the party reaches the boss room: an iron door with a lamp above it, burning red.
Raid leader Mok Hangyu, B-rank, explains the plan with the smile he uses for his streams. It's a simple plan, and it needs bait.
And this time the bait isn't the doll. It's Jaeha himself.
Jaeha keeps smiling. But he has been staring at that lamp since they arrived,
and three hundred and twelve raids have taught him what red means.
Mok's smile dies. He shoves Jaeha toward the door with his shield. Better run fast.
He already knows how this ends if they shut that door behind him.
Inside, a giant armoured knight kneels at the end of a vast hall, wrapped in broken chains.
Except the chains are modern factory steel, stamped and bolted. Someone was down here before the guild.
Jaeha takes one step in,
and a red light switches on inside the empty helmet.
The knight rises: four and a half metres of armour and sword.
That's the guild's cue. The hunters charge in from both sides, exactly as planned.
It doesn't go as planned.
One swing, and the attackers are down. This is no C-grade boss.
The next blow sends Mok skidding back behind his shield.
Behind a pillar, Jaeha does what he always does: he watches. Every boss has habits,
and he has already found one he can use.
Which is bad news for Yerin, frozen right in front of it.
Jaeha dives out and drags her behind the pillar as the sword smashes the floor where she stood.
Behind the pillar he keeps his voice low and calm. She is shaking too hard to stand.
And Mok? He gets his people out and leaves two behind to buy the time.
The door slams, and the bolt locks from outside.
Yerin can't believe they locked them in. Jaeha can.
And now the knight comes for them.
His hand won't stop shaking. Today's traps took every husk he had but the last.
The knight's free hand drags Yerin out by her bag strap, and the sword rises over her.
So he makes the call he has made three hundred and twelve times.
But this husk comes out wrong: cracked all over, glowing cyan, arms spread between Yerin and the blade.
Then something answers that has never answered him before: a window, glowing cyan in the dark.
It has been counting too. Not his kills. Something else.
An emergency call, it says, and his last husk is the price.
No time to ask. The sword comes down.
And someone answers. The husk bursts open, and a small cloaked goblin catches the giant blade on two crossed knives, a shard of the husk's face still over his eye like a mask.
The edge stops a finger's width from Yerin's eye.
Holding the boss's sword back one-handed, the goblin glances over his shoulder: who's in charge here?
And Jaeha, the trap rat with zero kills, raises one finger. I think... it's me?
